newsitem.title: UK: Refco sees lower 1997 sugar prices, but China key.
newsitem.headline: Refco sees lower 1997 sugar prices, but China key.

text.p: World raw sugar prices should test levels as low as nine cents/lb in 1997 but if China buys at the cheaper values, short-term fund aggression could push prices up to 12 cents, commission house Refco said in its annual review. "Not withstanding unforeseen technical aberrations...raw prices next year will be under pressure both constantly and frequently," the review said, adding that a price test of between 9.0 and 9.5 cents/lb looked "a distinct probability".
But the lower levels could trigger China's known need to buy sugar sometime next year and then fund players could fuel a price rally, Refco said.

"On current information, upside momentum looks severely limited -- the caveat to this is whether such low levels invite shrewd Chinese opportunism of a sufficient size to excite external participants," it said.
"In this respect fund aggression could easily raise world prices 200/300 points off such lows...as a short term phenomenon," it said, pegging an upside range of between 11.5 and 12.0 cents/lb.
Raw sugar for March delivery on the New York exchange is currently priced at around 10.70 cents/lb.
But technical rallies would be tenuous unless they were supported by the physical situation, widely seen as bearish for 1997 due to an abundant world surplus of sugar, Refco said.
"All things considered, we see no alternative but to remain cautiously on the bear track," it said.
The premium between white and raw sugar would narrow and drag the price of white sugar on the London exchange lower during the course of 1997, it added.
